title: APT and parrot-upgrade
description: Manage Debian-format packages and dependencies. Use `apt` interactively; use `apt-get`/`apt-cache` for stable scripting interfaces.

title: Bash and core shell commands
description: Navigate folders, create files and understand shell operators before combining tool commands. cd is a shell builtin; many file utilities come from coreutils.

title: GNOME Tweaks and extensions
description: Adjust GNOME desktop preferences beyond the standard Settings app. GNOME extensions require GNOME Shell; they do not apply to MATE/KDE.

title: Git
description: Track file history, inspect changes, and collaborate with a remote repository.

title: Python virtual environments
description: Keep project dependencies separate from Parrot’s system Python.

title: pip
description: Install Python libraries inside a project environment. Use `python -m pip` to select the pip belonging to that interpreter.

title: pipx
description: Install Python command-line applications into separate environments while exposing their commands on your PATH.

title: dpkg
description: Inspect and manage individual .deb packages and their installed file lists. APT sits above dpkg and resolves downloads/dependencies.

title: OpenVPN
description: Connect to a trusted VPN provider or lab using its issued profile and credentials.

title: ip
description: Inspect addresses, links, neighbors and routes using the modern iproute2 suite.

title: ss
description: Identify listening ports, active sockets and the processes that own them. Part of iproute2.

title: nmcli / NetworkManager
description: Inspect and manage connections controlled by NetworkManager. Distinguish a device from its saved connection profile.

title: dig
description: Query DNS records and inspect resolver answers. Both tools are supplied by BIND utilities on typical Debian-based installations.

title: nslookup
description: Query DNS records and inspect resolver answers. Both tools are supplied by BIND utilities on typical Debian-based installations.

title: getent
description: Query the system name-service configuration, including hosts files and DNS where configured.

title: sysctl
description: Inspect and deliberately change kernel runtime parameters. Most network failures do not require changing these settings.

title: Burp Suite Community
description: Intercept, inspect and replay HTTP requests in a dedicated browser testing workflow. Community is free; Professional is a separate licensed product.

title: tar
description: Create, list and extract archives; compression and archiving are separate steps combined by convenient options.

title: RouterSploit
description: Explore embedded-device module metadata in an isolated, firmware-specific lab. Historical dependencies may not support a modern Parrot release.

title: CrackMapExec migration
description: Understand older CME notes and move new workflows to NetExec without assuming command-line flags are identical.

title: NetExec
description: Assess protocol configuration and permitted account access in Windows/AD labs. The primary CLI is commonly nxc; verify installed entry points.

title: smbclient
description: Browse authorized Windows/Samba shares with an interactive client and prompted credentials.

title: CIFS mounts / cifs-utils
description: Mount an SMB share into the local filesystem with explicit permissions and a clear unmount step.

title: SMBMap
description: Summarize SMB shares and effective permissions for an authorized account.

title: Impacket
description: Python protocol libraries and example clients for Windows/SMB and related network protocols.

title: Nmap
description: Discover hosts, inspect ports and identify services within an explicitly authorized scope.

title: curl
description: Send HTTP requests and inspect responses without a browser.

title: Wget
description: Download a resource to a local file with clear filename and timeout controls.

title: Gobuster
description: Enumerate web paths, DNS names or virtual hosts with explicit mode-specific options.

title: SecLists
description: A collection of test wordlists for discovery and security exercises. It is data, not an executable scanner.

title: Nikto
description: Check web servers for known risky files, outdated components and configuration clues. Findings need manual validation.

title: Wfuzz
description: Fuzz paths or request parameters with payload generators and filters based on response properties.

title: ffuf
description: Replace a FUZZ marker in HTTP requests with wordlist entries, with calibration, rate limits and structured output.

title: PostgreSQL service for labs
description: Provide the optional database used by Metasploit workspaces. Service installation and database initialization are separate actions.

title: Metasploit Framework
description: Organize authorized testing modules and evidence in workspaces. Framework is distinct from licensed Metasploit Pro.

title: Meterpreter sessions
description: Interact with an existing authorized lab session using platform-supported commands. Meterpreter is a payload/session type, not an independent desktop package.

title: msfvenom
description: Inspect Framework payload metadata and supported output formats. Installed with Metasploit Framework.

title: Netcat / nc
description: Open simple TCP clients/listeners for local protocol and connection exercises. This guide targets netcat-openbsd, not every nc implementation.

title: OpenSSH / ssh and scp
description: Log in and copy files over encrypted authenticated connections. Client installation does not install an SSH server.

title: Python HTTP server
description: Temporarily serve a dedicated folder for local file inspection and download exercises. Not a production server.

title: Crunch
description: Generate candidate strings from an explicit character set for small controlled exercises. It does not authenticate or crack anything by itself.

title: Hydra
description: Test a small, agreed set of login attempts against a designated training account. Different protocols require different modules.

title: Medusa
description: Perform module-specific authentication checks in a bounded training environment. Use it as an alternative to Hydra, not a redundant extra run.

title: sqlmap
description: Validate suspected SQL injection in your own test application using a captured raw request and a single chosen parameter.

title: iw
description: Inspect modern Linux wireless interfaces, driver capabilities and connection state.

title: airmon-ng
description: Manage monitor-mode interfaces for supported Aircrack-ng hardware in an authorized wireless lab.

title: Wireshark
description: Inspect network packets visually with display filters and protocol detail panes.

title: tcpdump
description: Capture a narrowly filtered packet trace from a specific interface for diagnosis.

title: TShark
description: Use Wireshark protocol analysis from the terminal, especially for reading saved captures and extracting fields.

title: find
description: Locate filesystem entries by name, type, size and other metadata. It searches paths, not file contents.

title: less
description: Read long files without loading an editor; search and navigate logs interactively.

title: sha256sum
description: Calculate SHA-256 digests to compare file bytes or verify against a trusted publisher checksum.

title: jq
description: Read, transform and validate JSON using composable filters.

title: ripgrep / rg
description: Search file contents quickly with useful line numbers, file filters and explicit hidden-file handling.

title: tmux
description: Keep related terminal windows and panes in a session that survives client detachment.

title: btop
description: Monitor CPU, memory, disks, network rates and processes interactively.

title: OpenSSL
description: Inspect certificates and create local test cryptographic material without assuming that an arbitrary certificate is trusted.

title: OWASP ZAP
description: Inspect HTTP traffic and assess your own web application with a scoped proxy workflow. Passive analysis and active scans have different effects.

title: ShellCheck
description: Analyze shell scripts for common quoting, portability and logic mistakes without executing them.

title: systemctl
description: Inspect and control systemd units. Starting now and enabling at boot are separate operations.

title: journalctl
description: Read systemd journal entries by service, boot and time to diagnose the exact failure.
